meta.purpose: Source of truth for licensing content in MSU Tycoon. The game must not state licensing facts that are not here.
meta.pricesNote: No real prices appear here or in the game. All in-game money is fictional credits.
simplifications: The game computes R4HA from 5-minute intervals per LPAR; real SCRT also handles partial hours, LPAR moves and many edge cases.
Soft capping is modelled as a hard limit at the defined capacity; real WLM capping can briefly overshoot and uses capping patterns.
TFP Software Consumption is reduced to an annual baseline plus a year-end growth-rate true-up; real contracts are individually negotiated.

codex.definition: Millions of Service Units per hour: IBM's capacity rating for each machine model and the unit most z/OS software is priced in.
codex.inGame: Every LPAR's consumption and every bill is in MSU.

codex.definition: Rolling four-hour average MSU consumption of an LPAR.
codex.inGame: Mean of the last 48 five-minute intervals for each LPAR.

codex.definition: Eligible products are charged on the utilization of the LPARs where they run instead of the full machine capacity. For a sub-capacity MLC product, the month's highest R4HA across those LPARs sets the charge.
codex.inGame: Billed MSU = the product's highest hourly sum of LPAR R4HAs in the month.

codex.definition: A recurring monthly charge that includes the right to use the product and IBM support during the period. MLC capacity can go up or down each month.
codex.inGame: z/OS, Db2, CICS, IMS and MQ are MLC products billed monthly.

codex.definition: Advanced Workload License Charges, the sub-capacity MLC metric used for most z/OS software on current hardware, with a per-MSU price that falls through tiers as MSU rises.
codex.inGame: The default MLC model, with a fictional tier table.

codex.definition: Flat Workload License Charges: MLC products that aren't sub-capacity eligible pay a fixed monthly charge unrelated to capacity.
codex.inGame: Flat-charge products ignore MSU.

codex.definition: Select Application License Charges: lets IBM MQ be licensed on product utilization instead of the sub-capacity MLC metrics.
codex.inGame: Codex-only entry.

codex.definition: International Program License Agreement: a one-time charge for the licence plus annual Subscription and Support. For IPLA products, licensed capacity cannot decrease once purchased.
codex.inGame: Buying IPLA capacity is permanent; support is charged yearly on everything owned.

codex.definition: Must be licensed wherever a specific parent product (such as Db2, CICS or IMS) runs. Example: Db2 Sort for z/OS.
codex.inGame: A Db2 tool must cover every LPAR running Db2.

codex.definition: Licensed for the capacity of the LPARs where the product itself executes.
codex.inGame: Follows its own usage.

codex.definition: Licensed for the capacity of the LPARs where z/OS runs.
codex.inGame: Follows z/OS LPARs.

codex.definition: Sub-Capacity Reporting Tool. Processes SMF type 70 subtype 1 and SMF type 89 subtypes 1 and 2 from every z/OS LPAR on a CPC (SCRT89 records for z/TPF and z/VSE) and produces the monthly sub-capacity report.
codex.inGame: The monthly report screen is an SCRT-style report.

codex.definition: IBM's policy requires SCRT reports to be created with the most current SCRT version. Version 30.1.12 (20 May 2026) was the latest listed on 2026-11-05.
codex.inGame: Skipping an SCRT update flags the report non-compliant.

codex.definition: A soft cap on an LPAR. When the LPAR's R4HA exceeds it, WLM caps the LPAR, which limits the MSU that SCRT reports for it.
codex.inGame: Lowers the bill but defers work and risks SLA.

codex.definition: A soft cap shared by a group of LPARs on the same CPC, applied to their combined R4HA.
codex.inGame: One cap across several LPARs.

codex.definition: IBM Z pricing family that includes the Software Consumption Solution (formerly Enterprise Consumption), Enterprise Capacity Solution, Application Development and Test Solution, New Application Solution, and, since May 2021, the Hardware Consumption Solution.
codex.inGame: Available as a renewal choice.

codex.definition: Usage-based model where compute is measured on MSUs consumed (aggregated hourly) rather than the R4HA peak, removing the need for capping as a cost control. It uses an annual baseline with a growth rate for consumption above it.
codex.inGame: Baseline billed monthly; overage billed at year end; capping saves nothing.

codex.definition: A full-capacity licensing model aimed at maximum price predictability.
codex.inGame: Codex-only entry.

codex.definition: Product usage records written by products that register with z/OS. Processed by IFAURP for usage reporting and by SCRT.
codex.inGame: Column 2 of the Inventory Reconciler.

codex.definition: Parmlib member holding the product enablement policy. Activate with SET PROD=xx and point PROD= in IEASYSxx at it for the next IPL. Only products that call z/OS registration services are controlled by it; RACF/Security Server enablement only changes at IPL.
codex.inGame: Enable/disable products per LPAR. MQ can't be disabled this way.

codex.definition: IBM's z/OS SAM product: Inquisitor scans libraries, Usage Monitor records module use, the Global Knowledge Base identifies products, Analyzer reports. Requires z/OS 2.5 or later and Db2 or SQLite.
codex.inGame: The 'inventory scan' action.

codex.definition: Third-party vendors use IBM's SCRT with a vendor-supplied product catalog (Broadcom's is member CAS9SCRT) to produce their own sub-capacity reports. SCRT 30.1.12 can optionally report a checksum for an ISV catalog.
codex.inGame: Fictional vendors ask for these in audits.

codex.definition: Major ISVs price mainframe software on MSU or MIPS and offer consumption models: Broadcom Mainframe Consumption Licensing (MCL) and BMC zConsumption Licensing (zCL).
codex.inGame: Vendor A mirrors a capacity/MCL-style model; Vendor B mirrors an MSU-tier/zCL-style model.

codex.definition: Capacity-priced software follows MSU ratings, and new machine generations carry new ratings and larger full capacity. z/OS 3.2 runs on z17, z16 and z15.
codex.inGame: The upgrade event raises uncapped full-capacity contracts.

quiz.q: A sub-capacity MLC product's monthly bill is driven by…
options: The highest rolling 4-hour average MSU of the LPARs where it ran
The full MSU rating of the CPC
The number of LPARs it is enabled on
quiz.why: The month's peak R4HA on the LPARs where the product ran sets the charge, as reported by SCRT.

quiz.q: What does an MLC fee include?
options: Right to use plus IBM support for the period
quiz.why: MLC bundles use rights with support; IPLA separates the one-time licence from annual S&S.

quiz.q: Can IPLA licensed capacity be reduced after purchase?
quiz.why: MLC capacity can move monthly. IPLA capacity, once bought, cannot decrease.

quiz.q: A Db2 tool must be licensed wherever Db2 runs. Which IPLA model is that?
quiz.why: Reference-based products follow the parent product's LPARs.

quiz.q: Which MLC metric is a flat charge unrelated to CPC capacity?
quiz.why: Non-sub-capacity MLC products are FWLC: a fixed monthly charge.

quiz.q: Which SMF records does SCRT need from z/OS?
options: Type 70 subtype 1 and type 89 subtypes 1 and 2
quiz.why: SMF 70-1 gives CPU activity; SMF 89-1/2 gives product usage, from every z/OS LPAR on the CPC.

quiz.q: Which SCRT level must you use for IBM reports?
options: Any version from the last 12 months
The version shipped with your z/OS release
Whatever IBM approved at contract signing
quiz.why: IBM's policy requires reports made with the current SCRT.

quiz.q: What does a defined capacity do?
options: Soft-caps the LPAR when its R4HA exceeds the limit
quiz.why: WLM caps the LPAR so its reported MSU stays near the limit.

quiz.q: Under TFP Software Consumption, what replaces the monthly R4HA peak?
options: MSU consumed, aggregated hourly, against an annual baseline
quiz.why: Consumption pricing charges on MSU consumed, so capping isn't needed for cost control.

quiz.q: In what year was the Hardware Consumption Solution added to TFP?
quiz.why: TFP began for software in 2019; the Hardware Consumption Solution was announced in May 2021.

quiz.q: How do you activate an IFAPRDxx change without an IPL?
quiz.why: SET PROD=xx activates it now; update PROD= in IEASYSxx for the next IPL.

quiz.q: Why can't IFAPRDxx disable IBM MQ on an LPAR?
options: MQ doesn't call z/OS product registration services
quiz.why: Only products designed to call registration services are controlled by IFAPRDxx.

quiz.q: Which utility processes SMF type 89 records for usage reporting?
quiz.why: IFAURP processes sorted type 89 records with the history file.

quiz.q: Which IZSAM component scans libraries to build inventory?
quiz.why: Inquisitor scans; Usage Monitor records use; GKB identifies; Analyzer reports.

quiz.q: How do ISV SCRT reports identify vendor products?
options: A vendor-supplied product catalog fed to IBM's SCRT
quiz.why: Vendors ship a product catalog that IBM's SCRT uses to build the ISV report.

quiz.q: Why can a hardware upgrade raise software cost with flat workload?
options: New models carry new MSU ratings and larger full capacity
quiz.why: Capacity-priced software follows MSU ratings; contracts without caps can rise with the machine.

auditCards.finding: A Db2 tool is licensed (reference-based) for LPARs A and B. Db2 was just stood up on LPAR C.
auditCards.why: Reference-based products follow the parent; Db2 on LPAR C extends the tool's licence scope.

auditCards.finding: A test job on the dev LPAR uses an MLC product that is otherwise unused there, and SCRT now counts that LPAR.
auditCards.why: Remove the stray use and that LPAR's R4HA stops counting for the product.

auditCards.finding: Last month's SCRT report was produced with a version from a year ago.
auditCards.why: IBM requires the current SCRT level.

auditCards.finding: Inventory shows an ISV product with zero usage for 12 months; renewal is in six months.
auditCards.why: Unused software before renewal is a removal or reduction candidate.

auditCards.finding: You keep 24 months of SCRT reports with the SMF 70/89 input that produced them.
auditCards.why: That's the evidence an auditor asks for first.

auditCards.finding: An ISV product is licensed sub-capacity, but nobody kept the ISV SCRT reports.
auditCards.why: Without reports you can't prove sub-capacity use, and the vendor can claim full capacity.

auditCards.finding: Month-end batch sets the R4HA peak; it could run four hours later when the system is quiet.
auditCards.why: Moving work out of the peak window lowers billed R4HA for every MLC product on those LPARs.

auditCards.finding: A priced z/OS feature shows as enabled in IFAPRDxx, but it was never ordered.
auditCards.why: An enabled priced feature you didn't order is a compliance gap.

auditCards.finding: Two tape management systems are licensed for the same job.
auditCards.why: Duplicate tools are a classic rationalization target.

auditCards.finding: The team plans to 'unlicense' IBM MQ on an LPAR by disabling it in IFAPRDxx.
auditCards.why: MQ doesn't use product registration, so IFAPRDxx won't stop it.

auditCards.finding: Entitlements, the SCRT product list and the IFAPRDxx policy all agree this month.
auditCards.why: Three sources lining up is the target state.

auditCards.finding: An ISV contract is priced on full capacity with no cap, and a hardware upgrade is planned.
auditCards.why: New MSU ratings can raise the bill with flat workload. Negotiate a cap first.

auditCards.finding: Under TFP Software Consumption, the team removes soft caps on production LPARs.
auditCards.why: Consumption pricing means caps aren't needed for cost control.
